subject: Security notification and request: auth spike + SOC 2 evidence and postmortem sharing
messages:
From: Everledger Security <security-team@everledger.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Alert - short-lived auth spike detected (request: IRP + evidence)

Hi Markus / Marissa / Jonas,

We detected an unusual authentication spike against Everledger org keys that touched a small subset of sessions used to call your hosted inference endpoints. We've triaged this as an elevated-risk telemetry event (no confirmed data exfil).

Summary:
- Time window: 2026-09-02 14:07:10 -> 14:12:40 UTC
- Affected API keys: masked (will provide mapping)
- Observed behavior: rapid token reuse from three IPs, some anomalous user-agents

What we need from Redwood (priority):
1) Confirmation of whether this maps to a known maintenance/job or unexpected client behavior.
2) Incident Response Plan (IRP) excerpt that explains Redwood's notification cadence and evidence delivery process for SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ requests.
3) Forensics artifacts: request that you provide request logs, authentication logs, session traces covering the 14:00-14:30 UTC window and any associated redaction guidance for public postmortem sharing.

We have uploaded our initial alert screenshot and a short manifest to a shared Drive folder (link below). Alex Rivera (cc) will own follow-ups from Everledger side.

Attachments: initial_alert_screenshot.png
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cEverledgerEvidence

Can you acknowledge receipt and provide an estimated timeline for evidence handoff? Everledger's compliance team would like a redacted postmortem within 5 business days if possible.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Incident Lead, Everledger Security
security-team@everledger.com

---
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Everledger Security <security-team@everledger.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alert - short-lived auth spike detected (request: IRP + evidence)

Thanks Alex — acknowledged.

Marking this as an ongoing investigation. Quick notes / next steps from our side: 
- We will identify the exact API key mapping and gather the request logs for 2026-09-02 14:00-14:30 UTC.
- Marissa will pull the authentication and KV-cache access traces, Jonas will coordinate forensic export and any needed PII redaction.
- Target ETA for a first artifact bundle: EOD (UTC) 2026-09-02. Redacted postmortem to follow in 3 business days; we'll let you know if we need an extension.

Marissa / Jonas — please confirm you can meet the EOD artifact ETA; call if you need more time. Jonas, please open a JIRA under SEC-4129 and attach the export when ready.

Markus Klein

Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Alert - short-lived auth spike detected (request: IRP + evidence)

Hi Markus — thanks for the quick ack. That timeline sounds fine. A couple clarifying asks: 
1) Please include the list of IPs observed in your logs and whether any of them map to known Redwood maintenance ranges.
2) We need an artifact manifest that maps file names to the log types and a checksum (we've included ours in the Drive folder).
3) For the postmortem, Everledger compliance will need a CAIQ/SIG mapping that shows which controls were exercised during containment/forensics (high level is fine).

I uploaded three artifacts from our side to the Drive folder and included presigned S3 links (short lived): auth_spike.log.gz, session_dump.ndjson, forensics_manifest.csv. 

Would Redwood be able to provide: request logs (redwood-request-logs-20260902-1400-1430.gz), auth table extract, and a redaction-ready postmortem draft? We can coordinate a secure SFTP or use the Drive folder — whichever fits Redwood's evidence ingestion policy.

Thanks again,
Alex Rivera
Incident Lead, Everledger Security
attachments: auth_spike.log.gz; session_dump.ndjson; forensics_manifest.csv

Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alert - short-lived auth spike detected (request: IRP + evidence)

Alex / Everledger — attaching the artifact handoff and an initial redaction-friendly postmortem (PDF). See the Drive link below for encrypted archives.

What we provided:
- redacted_postmortem_v1.pdf (high-level timeline, root cause hypothesis, actions taken; sensitive identifiers redacted)
- redwood-request-logs-20260902-1400-1430.gz (server-side request logs; hashes included in manifest)
- auth_table_extract_20260902.csv (auth events verified during window)

For transfer: we've staged an encrypted tar on our SFTP (details in Drive file "transfer_instructions.txt"). If Everledger prefers our S3 presigned approach we can generate short-lived links.

Notes on SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ mapping: for the containment run we exercised controls in the following families: CC6 (access monitoring), CC7 (incident response), and CC8 (change control for ephemeral key rotation). We'll compile a short mapping doc that ties the actions in the postmortem to expected SIG/CAIQ responses and share by EOD 2026-09-04.

Attachments: redacted_postmortem_v1.pdf; transfer_instructions.txt
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cEverledgerEvidence
Jira: SEC-4129

If you'd like a quick walk-through of the artifacts, Jonas and I are available this afternoon 17:00-18:00 UTC. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Operations
Redwood Inference
